chunks: And informed me Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man and al-Husayn ibn Ubayd Allah from Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Safwani, saying:

The Shaykh Abul-Qasim (may Allah be pleased with him) bequeathed his authority to Abul-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Samurri (may Allah be pleased with him), so he undertook the duties that were incumbent upon Abul-Qasim. When death approached him, the Shia gathered around him and asked him about the one appointed after him and who would take his place, but he did not reveal anything regarding that and mentioned that he had not been ordered to appoint anyone after him in this matter.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ عَلِيُّ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ ا: Abul-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Samurri, the deputy of the Imam
key_terms.أَبُو الْقَاسِمُ: Abul-Qasim, a key figure in the Ghaybah period

ai.seo_question: Who did Shaykh Abul-Qasim appoint as his successor and what did al-Samurri say about his own succession?
ai.summary: This narration highlights the transitional phase of the Minor Exile (al-Ghurba al-Sughra), where Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh, the fourth and final deputy of the Twelfth Imam, designated Ali ibn Muhammad al-Samurri as his successor. Upon Abu al-Qasim's death, al-Samurri clarified that he was not commanded to appoint a specific successor for this particular role, thereby marking the end of the four-deputy system and the beginning of the period of general waiting (al-Intizar al-Amm) until the Major Exile.
